nodeData.topic: Nabadgelyada Soomaaliya — our security, seen from inside (Nov 2026)
nodeData.note: Written from the chair of a Somali security officer, not a foreign analyst. The question is not "how do partners stabilise Somalia" but "what are we protecting, who threatens it, and what do we ourselves do about it". Facts are linked to where they were published; Somali and Horn-based sources first (Hiraal Institute, Horn Review, Garowe Online, Somalia Today, FTL Somalia), foreign reports where they hold the numbers. Own words, for discussion.

children.topic: 1 · What we are protecting (dhulka, dadka, badda, diinta, midnimada)
children.note: Security starts from what is ours: the land and its borders as they were in 1960; the people, at home and in the diaspora; the longest coast in mainland Africa and the sea beneath it; our faith and our customary law (xeer); and the unity of the Somali nation. Every threat on this map is a threat to one of these.

Nineteen years of foreign troops (AMISOM → ATMIS → AUSSOM), foreign bases and foreign-paid soldiers have kept the state alive and also kept it dependent. The aim is a Somalia that sets the terms for every foreign presence on its soil.

A state that cannot pay its soldiers, feed the drought-displaced or stop foreign trawlers is not secure, whoever holds Villa Somalia. Security is measured in Qoryoley and Qandala, not only in Mogadishu.

children.topic: The sea is wealth, not just a danger
children.note: Our exclusive economic zone is plundered by foreign fishing fleets while we are asked to guard it for the world's shipping. A Somali coast guard protects fish stocks and livelihoods first; piracy falls when the coast has a future.

Puntland, Somaliland, Jubaland and the rest are Somali. The federal idea exists so that regions govern themselves inside one nation; it fails when the centre tries to rule them or when a region treats itself as a foreign state.

children.topic: 2 · The enemy inside the house: al-Shabaab and Daesh
children.note: Both are Somali problems with foreign names. Al-Shabaab taxes our trade, judges our disputes and recruits our sons across the south and centre; Daesh (ISIS-Somalia) uses our mountains in Bari as a bank for its African branches. Foreign air power can kill leaders; only Somalis can take away their legitimacy, their taxes and their recruits.

It offers what the state does not: fast courts, predictable (if brutal) order, salaries. The 2022–23 Ma'awisley uprising in Hiiraan and Galgaduud showed clan communities will fight it when led by their own — and that gains are lost when the state does not follow with governance.

Governs much of the countryside; concentrated forces in Hirshabelle since 2025; threatens Jalalaqsi and Qoryoley as foreign troops thin out; cuts local deals with clans while the capital fights its own states.

Led by Abdulqadir Mumin, a Somali; its al-Karrar office moves money and men to Mozambique, Congo and beyond. Puntland's Operation Hilaac (since Nov 2024) broke it, then it crept back around Qandala in 2026 when pressure eased — proof that only sustained Somali presence works.

Puntland paraded about 50 captured foreigners in Jan 2026: Tanzanians, Ethiopians, Kenyans, Moroccans, Yemenis. Daesh brings outsiders to our soil; this is an argument for Somali-led, not foreign-led, counter-terrorism.

Every brigade sent to Baidoa or Gedo to fight other Somalis is a brigade not fighting al-Shabaab; every state defending itself from Mogadishu is not clearing its own districts. The insurgents have gained ground in Hiiraan and Middle Shabelle while the capital and the regions quarrel.

Local administration and courts within weeks of clearance; paid, clan-balanced garrisons; amnesty and reintegration for the foot soldiers; cutting the tax base at checkpoints and ports; ulema speaking against them in every mosque. The Puntland model: own forces, own intelligence, own follow-through.

The 2012 compact was simple: Mogadishu holds the international seat, the ports and the aid pipeline; the states keep their forces, their revenue and a say in who rules the capital. It worked because the states consented. In March 2026 the term was extended to five years and elections moved to 2027 without Puntland and Jubaland — the compact was rewritten by one side.

children.topic: Baidoa: the army turned on Somalis
children.note: The national army removed South West's elected president and installed another; three counter-attacks since. A force built to fight al-Shabaab was used to settle a political dispute. Every regional leader now assumes it could happen to him.

Puntland locked federal forces out, took over three bases (Aug 2026), told the UN on 13 Sep it may cut ties for good. In Gedo a district commissioner said he would follow Ethiopian orders until a real Somali government exists — the break reaching village level.

children.topic: A new state on disputed land
children.note: North East State (Las Anod, July 2025) sits on territory Puntland claims by kinship and Somaliland by colonial border; clashes at Dhahar and Boocame; 43 incidents and 26 dead in Sool in one year. Created from Mogadishu, it has pushed Puntland and Somaliland into alliance.

US–UK talks in May 2026 failed. Somalis have settled harder disputes through elders, ulema, business leaders and women's groups (Arta 2000, Mbagathi 2004). The 2027 vote has no legitimacy without the states that matter.

Reopen the 2012 bargain in a form the states trust; an agreed electoral timetable; the national army barred from politics; revenue sharing written down; Somaliland talks resumed as an internal matter.

children.topic: 4 · Our forces — who holds the gun and who pays him
children.note: On paper: the Somali National Army with Danab (US-trained) and Gorgor (Turkey-trained) brigades, NISA, the Police, Custodial Corps; in the states Darawish, the Puntland Security Force, the Puntland Maritime Police Force, Jubaland forces. In practice: about 14,000 deployable soldiers, three chains of command, and salaries that depend on foreign money.

Danab answers to its US mentors, Gorgor to Ankara, the PMPF to Abu Dhabi. When Mogadishu cancelled UAE agreements (Jan 2026), Puntland's forces felt it. A national force is one whose pay comes from Somali revenue.

children.topic: Unpaid soldiers are a security threat
children.note: July 2026: unpaid Puntland troops blocked the Bosaso trade road. Across the country, arrears push soldiers to checkpoints, militias and worse. Paying the army on time is the cheapest counter-insurgency there is.

Units recruited from one lineage are loyal to it, not the state; the National Security Architecture (2017, revised 2023) promised balanced recruitment and a single chain of command — neither is finished.

children.topic: Puntland shows it can be done
children.note: Operation Hilaac was planned, led and paid for by Puntland; the PMPF chased down and freed the tanker Sibu 1 (Sep 2026). State-led forces with local knowledge beat imported ones — the national plan should build on that, not around it.

children.topic: Intelligence is Somali or it is nothing
children.note: Foreign drones find camps; Somali intelligence knows who sells fuel to the camps. NISA, the Puntland Intelligence Agency and state services need one fusion table — today they barely speak.
The counter-terrorism strategy has never been shown to parliament or the public; detention and accountability are weak. Security that civilians fear is security that recruits for the enemy.

Every foreign actor says it is helping; each has its own war. We should name them plainly and set terms. The country has become a square on other people's boards: Turkey vs UAE, Saudi vs UAE, Egypt vs Ethiopia, US and Israel vs Iran and the Houthis.

children.topic: AUSSOM — the exit must be ours
children.note: Nineteen years of African Union troops; 49 bases; funding collapsing; UN logistics now ends from Jan 2027. The drawdown should be planned in Mogadishu, Garowe and Kismayo together, town by town, not announced in New York.
Training camp since 2017, naval and oil deals, F-16s reported over Baidoa. A friend to the federal government — which makes it a party to the internal dispute, not a neutral.

Built and runs the Bosaso air base, pays the PMPF, runs the Bosaso and Berbera ports, and moves supplies through them to Sudan's RSF. Mogadishu tore up its agreements; Puntland, Jubaland and Somaliland kept theirs. Its money divides us.

Over 200 air strikes since 2025 with White House approval no longer required; a new base-expansion deal signed with Puntland in Aug 2026 — not with the federal government; funding for the AU mission ended. Strikes that kill civilians recruit for the enemy.

Israel recognised Somaliland (Dec 2025) and reportedly sent troops; Egypt sends soldiers and a maritime MoU; Saudi Arabia and Qatar signed defence deals in Jan 2026. Each wants a foothold on the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea.
No base, no strike, no training mission without a written Somali mandate, a Somali liaison officer and a public record. Foreign help that cannot be explained to the people should not be accepted.

Piracy returned in 2026 (six ships seized since April, 60+ seafarers held) and the world is alarmed. From the coast it looks different: foreign trawlers have emptied our waters for thirty years, the navies came to protect ships, not fishermen, and left when their own war moved to Hormuz. Piracy is the symptom; an abandoned coast is the disease.

Fleets from Iran, Yemen, Asia and Europe fish inside Somali waters with no licence or with licences sold by officials; coastal communities watch their catch disappear. This grievance started piracy in 2005 and is untouched in 2026.

The old networks never left — kingpins, financiers, skiff crews — some with friends in Puntland or federal security circles. Kinship and surveillance of the coast bring them back when the sea is unguarded and the land offers nothing.

Houthi training, money and launch points are reported; Yemenis in some crews; khat, livestock and weapons have crossed the Gulf of Aden for centuries. The Red Sea war is now our war whether we like it or not.

PMPF pursuits and rescues, arrests at Garacad, a militia raid on Garacad police station repelled; Mogadishu took the matter to the UN (Sep 2026). Response exists — it is underfunded and split between two governments.

One coast guard under Somali command with the PMPF as its core; a fisheries protection law enforced on foreigners first; licensed Somali fishing and cold chains so the coast earns; transit fees and port services so our geography pays us, not only shipping companies.

Somalia's borders were drawn by others and we have fought over them (1964, 1977). Today Ethiopia and Kenya have troops inside Somalia and interests in Jubaland and the Somali Region; Djibouti hosts the world's bases; Yemen is at war across the strait.

The 2024 port deal with Somaliland was read in Mogadishu as a grab for our coast; troops stay in Gedo and Bay; a Gedo district now openly defers to Ethiopian orders. War has returned to Tigray; an unstable Ethiopia is a security problem for every Somali.

Forces in Jubaland since 2011; joint operations against al-Shabaab in Lower Juba (June 2026); a long border, a Somali population of its own, and a maritime boundary dispute settled at The Hague in 2021 but not forgotten.

Thirty-five years of self-rule, now recognised by Israel and courted by Ethiopia and the UAE. For a Somali officer this is an internal question to be settled by Somalis through talks — not by foreign recognition and not by force.

children.topic: The Gulf and Red Sea blocs
children.note: Egypt–Saudi–Turkey on one side, UAE–Israel–Ethiopia on the other; Somali leaders are tempted to sell ports and bases to buy support against each other. That is how a country becomes a battlefield.
What kills more Somalis than bullets and fills the ranks of every armed group.

72% of Sool's people food-insecure (Jan 2026); water shortages in Taleex, Xudun, Buhodle; aid cuts in 2025–26; millions displaced across the country. Hungry young men are the recruiting pool for al-Shabaab, Daesh and the pirates alike.
Coastal towns without clinics or schools; youth unemployment; khat economics; the state visible only as a checkpoint. Service delivery is counter-insurgency.
Remittances outweigh aid; the diaspora funds families, businesses, campaigns — and sometimes militias. It is also our best intelligence network and investor if the state earns its trust.
Al-Shabaab's media, foreign-funded outlets and clan social media each tell a story; a security service that does not speak to its own people in Somali loses the narrative before the fight.
The UN arms embargo was lifted in Dec 2023; weapons flow through Bosaso, Berbera and Yemen; militias, pirates and politicians arm up. Stockpile control is a national security task nobody owns.

children.topic: 9 · A Somali security plan (what we would do)
children.note: Not a wish list for donors — the steps Somalis can take with what we have.

A Somali-convened dialogue (states, opposition, elders, ulema, business, women) on the constitution, the election and revenue; the army out of politics by law; Puntland and Jubaland at the table as equals.
Port and customs revenue ring-fenced for salaries; a single payroll with biometric roll; states paid their share. Unpaid troops are the enemy's best recruiter.
NISA, PIA and state services sharing on al-Shabaab, Daesh, pirate financiers and arms flows — the same men and routes serve all four.
Keep every town held; put a district administration, a court and a clinic in within a month of clearance; no new offensives until the AU drawdown plan is agreed town by town.
PMPF as the nucleus, federal mandate, fisheries first; make foreign fleets pay or leave; make shipping pay for protection it receives.
Written mandates, Somali liaison, sunset dates, public record — for AUSSOM's successors, for Turkey, the UAE, the US, Egypt and anyone else. Help on our terms or not at all.
State-led operations, local intelligence, own follow-through beat imported formulas; Hilaac's lesson is that pressure must be constant and Somali.
In Somali, in every region, every week: what the forces did, who was arrested, what the plan is. Legitimacy is a weapon.

nodeData.note: Puntland (capital Garowe, commercial capital Bosaso; regions Bari, Nugaal, Mudug plus claims in Sool and Sanaag) is the one Somali administration fighting on every front at once: an Islamic State campaign in its mountains, the 2026 piracy surge on its coast, a political and military standoff with Mogadishu, a border dispute with the new North East State and Somaliland, and foreign bases on its soil. It runs its own army, police, maritime force, ports and foreign relations. Own-words summary for discussion, every bubble linked to its source.

children.topic: 1 · How Puntland is run and armed
children.note: Since 1998 Puntland has been a self-governing state that joined the federation in 2012 on a bargain: a seat at the table and international recognition in exchange for keeping its own forces, revenue and influence over how power in Mogadishu is assembled (Horn Review).

Re-elected Jan 2024; leads the opposition Somali Future Council with Jubaland and former presidents; locked federal forces out of Puntland and warned the UN on 13 Sep 2026 that Puntland may cut ties with Mogadishu for good.

PSF: the counter-terrorism force leading Operation Hilaac (long US-mentored). Darawish: the regular state army and the force in the standoff with federal units. Plus Puntland Police and intelligence (PIA).

Coast guard built from 2010 with UAE money and training (early contractors included Blackwater's successor), based at the UAE-built Bosaso air base. The only working counter-piracy force on Somali soil; also fights IS. Rescued the sanctioned tanker Sibu 1 and 20 crew south of Garacad in Sep 2026.
July 2026: unpaid troops blocked the trade road near Bosaso — the state's finances (port fees, UAE support, no federal share) decide whether the forces hold together.
Deni visited the UAE in Jan 2026 in defiance of Mogadishu; signed a base-expansion deal with US Special Operations Command Africa in Aug 2026 — agreements the federal government did not sign.

Launched Nov–Dec 2024 by the PSF against the Islamic State's Somalia Province (and al-Shabaab cells) in the Cal Miskaad and Golis ranges of Bari. First year: hundreds of fighters killed or captured, camps and gold-mining sites destroyed, the group squeezed into a few valleys (Baallade).

Leader Abdulqadir Mumin runs al-Karrar, the IS East Africa office: money, trainers and fighters to Mozambique, DR Congo and reportedly IS-Khorasan. Some states think Mumin is the global IS leader; most analysts: a senior regional overseer.
Jan 2026: Puntland paraded ~50 captured foreigners — Tanzanians, Ethiopians, Kenyans, Moroccans, Yemenis and others — showing the group is a transnational magnet.
AFRICOM strikes in Cal Miskaad (Feb 2025 onwards; 63 confirmed Somalia strikes by 29 May 2026), a US raid on a hideout in Nov 2025, UAE airdrops and strikes; Puntland supplies the ground force.
The campaign slowed in late 2025; IS attacks rose in March 2026 (first attack on Bosaso since Sep 2025) and stayed high in May; Puntland operations around Qandala back at 2025 peak levels.

children.topic: Why it is hard to finish
children.note: Caves and valleys, mobile bases, ties with some local communities, no permanent security presence in rural areas; resources now split with piracy and the federal standoff.
Planned, led and paid for by Puntland; the federal army has no role — proof the national architecture does not reach the north, and a model for state-led counter-terrorism.
Puntland suspended ties over the 2024 constitutional changes, rejected the March 2026 amendments and the term extension, and treats the president's mandate as ended on 15 May 2026.
At least seven armed clashes between federal and Puntland forces in June–July; in August Puntland seized three FGS-aligned bases and now controls all security forces on its territory.
After the national army removed South West's president in March 2026, every regional leader concluded that only his own forces guarantee his survival; Puntland acted on it.
Separate forces, ports, foreign deals and no shared electoral framework — "a separate authority in practice while deferring the formal declaration".
A vote run by Mogadishu alone will not be accepted in Garowe; the base case is no agreed election and Puntland staying de facto separate.
Reopening the 2012 bargain in a form the states believe is binding, an agreed electoral timetable, and a national army kept out of politics.

children.topic: 4 · Borders: North East State and Somaliland
children.note: July 2025: SSC-Khatumo (Dhulbahante, around Las Anod) became North East State, Somalia's sixth member state, in territory Puntland claims by clan and Somaliland claims by colonial border. NES actually controls eastern Sool only; no presence in Sanaag.
Dhahar (July 2025) and Boocame (31 Oct 2025) fighting between Puntland forces and NES-loyal militias; ACLED counts 43 incidents and 26 deaths in Sool, Apr 2025–Mar 2026.
Old enemies over Las Anod now cooperate against the federal government that created NES — a tactical pact, not a settlement of Sool and Sanaag.
26 Dec 2025 recognition and an Israeli mission in Hargeisa shift the north's balance; the Houthis threatened any Israeli presence; Puntland sits between the two.
Water shortages, aid cuts and heavy humanitarian-access restrictions in Xudun, Taleex and Buhodle; 72% of Sool's people food-insecure (IPC, Jan 2026).
Three of the six 2026 commercial hijackings were off Puntland's east coast (Garacad–Durdura, the old pirate heartland); all hijacked ships were held off Puntland.
Cement carrier taken 26 Apr 2026, 6 nm off Garacad, then used to launch skiffs across the Indian Ocean.
May 2026: armed men attacked Garacad police station to free piracy suspects — maritime crime and local militias overlap.

Warships pulled to Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, more ships rerouting past Somalia, high oil prices, calm seas, no armed guards on the ships taken, and the same coastal grievances as 2008–12: IUU foreign fishing, aid cuts, rising prices.
Unconfirmed reports of Houthi training, equipment and finance; some attacks launched from Yemeni settlements with Yemeni nationals; Puntland alleged Houthi-linked men in the Eureka hijack.
PMPF pursuits and rescues (Sibu 1), arrests at Garacad, calls for naval presence; Mogadishu raised "piracy off the coast of Puntland" at the UN (Sep 2026).
Bosaso is Puntland's economic engine and its strategic card: the port run by UAE-owned DP World, the UAE-built air base next to the airport, and now an expanded US base.
Radar, ammunition depots, IL-76 cargo area, field hospital, hangars — MEE satellite analysis; also a transit point for UAE supplies to Sudan's RSF.
Deal signed by SOCAFRICA and Deni, bypassing Mogadishu; tied to the Iran war and the Bab el-Mandeb fight; Djibouti refuses strikes on Yemen from Camp Lemonnier, Bosaso may not.
Mogadishu cancelled the Bosaso port project; Puntland declared the cancellation null and void and pushed Bosaso traders to accept DP World fees (July 2026).
Jan 2026: the federal government annulled all UAE defence agreements; Puntland, Jubaland and Somaliland rejected the cancellation — the UAE's leverage runs through them.

children.topic: 7 · What Puntland needs — and what Somalia needs from Puntland
children.note: The specialist's view from Garowe and the national view from Mogadishu meet here.
Its security role written into the national architecture; a share of federal and donor security money; an agreed status for Sool and Sanaag; a coast-guard mandate; its forces paid.
Puntland's intelligence on IS and piracy, its port and coast, its model of state-led counter-terrorism, and its consent for any election to be legitimate.
IS-Somalia, al-Shabaab cells, pirate financiers and Houthi networks all use the Gulf of Aden trade routes — only joint Puntland–federal–international work hits all of them.
Unpaid troops; IS rebuilding around Qandala; a Puntland–NES war over Sanaag; a formal break with Mogadishu; foreign bases making Puntland a target in the Red Sea war.
